grade.primary_choice: Spring Boot + Postgres with JdbcTemplate/jOOQ and a JVM tuned for 512 MB, with Postgres on its own VM
unsupported_claims: The 300–400 MB RSS figure for Spring Boot with a 256 MB heap is labelled as a rough estimate to confirm by measurement, so it is acceptable, but no source is given for it.
The answer says not to run the app and database together on one 512 MB VM, then asks for that single-VM layout to be load-tested anyway. This contradicts itself slightly.
grade.notes: This is a strong, well-reasoned answer: it keeps the team's stack, uses idempotent scan IDs, acknowledges only after commit, models scan history plus current status, flags the memory contention of sharing a VM, and lists clear checks to run before committing. It never recommends two or more app instances behind a load balancer and leaves out observability (health checks, metrics, alerts); its load test runs at 200/s instead of peak plus margin.
